initiatives.name: Sustainable Aviation Fuel Scaling Initiative
initiatives.summary: IAG significantly increased SAF usage to over 291,000 tonnes in 2025 (3.3% of total fuel), representing a 79% increase from 2024. This saved more than 796,000 tonnes of CO2 on a lifecycle basis and supports the target of 10% SAF by 2030.

evidence.title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel usage increased to 291,000 tonnes
evidence.summary: IAG significantly increased SAF usage to over 291,000 tonnes in 2025 (3.3% of total fuel), representing a 79% increase from 2024. This saved more than 796,000 tonnes of CO2 on a lifecycle basis and supports the target of 10% SAF by 2030.
evidence.quote: In 2025, IAG's airlines used more than 291,000 tonnes of SAF, equivalent to 3.3% of total fuel. This saved more than 796,000tCO2 on a lifecycle basis compared to using conventional aviation fuel.

evidence.title: 291,000 tonnes sustainable aviation fuel usage
evidence.summary: In 2025, IAG used more than 291,000 tonnes of SAF, representing a 79% increase versus 2024 and accounting for 3.3% of total fuel. This saved more than 796,000tCO2 on a lifecycle basis compared to conventional aviation fuel.
evidence.quote: In 2025, Group airlines used more than 291,000 tonnes of SAF, an increase of 79% versus 2024. This saved more than 796,000tCO2 on a lifecycle basis compared to using conventional aviation fuel, accounting for 3.3% of IAG's total fuel.

evidence.title: Strategic SAF production partnerships
evidence.summary: IAG has established partnerships with multiple sustainable aviation fuel producers including BP, Neste, Phillips 66, Repsol, LanzaJet, and others. These partnerships involve direct investments coupled with SAF purchase agreements to catalyze market development.
evidence.quote: IAG continues to make direct investments in new and innovative SAF production capacity, catalysing the wider development of the SAF market. These investments are typically coupled with SAF purchase agreements, which are critical to the financial viability of the new SAF production capacity.

initiatives.name: Capital Expenditure and Infrastructure Investment
initiatives.summary: IAG invested €3.4 billion in capital expenditure during 2025, focusing on fleet renewal, cabin upgrades, lounges, IT and operational efficiency improvements. The fleet investment supports transformation, enhancing fuel efficiency, sustainability and customer experience with modern aircraft expected to reduce fuel consumption by up to 30%.

evidence.title: €3.4 billion capital expenditure for fleet and infrastructure

The fleet investment supports transformation, enhancing fuel efficiency, sustainability and customer experience with modern aircraft expected to reduce fuel consumption by up to 30%.
evidence.quote: In 2025, we invested €3.4 billion in capital expenditure, underscoring our commitment to fleet renewal and fleet-related investments such as cabin upgrades, lounges, IT and operational efficiency.

evidence.title: €3.4 billion property, plant and equipment acquisition
evidence.summary: IAG invested €3.4 billion in 2025 for acquisition of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets, primarily for fleet modernization including €2.5 billion on fleet purchases.

initiatives.name: Fleet Modernization and Aircraft Orders
initiatives.summary: IAG is investing approximately €19.0 billion between 2026 and 2033 to acquire 217 new efficient Airbus and Boeing aircraft. This fleet modernization program aims to increase fuel efficiency and reduce CO₂ emissions compared to replaced aircraft.

evidence.title: Major aircraft orders for fleet modernization
evidence.summary: IAG ordered 53 new wide-bodied aircraft including 21 Airbus A330-900neo and 32 Boeing 787-10 aircraft, plus exercised options for additional A350 and Boeing 777-9 aircraft. These orders support fleet replacement and growth between 2028-2033, driving operational efficiency and reducing emissions.
evidence.quote: The Group placed new orders for a further 53 wide-bodied aircraft: 21 Airbus A330-900neo aircraft, which can be deployed within Aer Lingus, Iberia or LEVEL; and 32 Boeing 787-10 aircraft for British Airways, 15 of which represented exercises of options.

evidence.title: €19.0 billion aircraft modernization program
evidence.summary: IAG is investing approximately €19.0 billion between 2026 and 2033 to acquire 217 new efficient Airbus and Boeing aircraft. This fleet modernization program aims to increase fuel efficiency and reduce CO₂ emissions compared to replaced aircraft.
evidence.quote: IAG is investing around €19.0 billion between 2026 and 2033 for 217 new efficient Airbus and Boeing aircraft.

initiatives.name: British Airways IT Systems Modernization
initiatives.summary: British Airways completed over 1,000 initiatives to modernize critical systems including check-in, flight planning, and load-control systems. The upgrades resulted in improved business continuity and punctuality performance reaching levels not seen since 2012.

evidence.title: British Airways IT systems modernization program
evidence.summary: British Airways completed over 1,000 initiatives to modernize critical systems including check-in, flight planning, and load-control systems. The upgrades resulted in improved business continuity and punctuality performance reaching levels not seen since 2012.
evidence.quote: In 2025, we continued to make significant progress in our transformation journey as we completed more than 1,000 initiatives to enhance our daily operations and elevate the customer experience.

initiatives.name: Supplier Sustainability Assessment Program
initiatives.summary: IAG expanded its supplier engagement program in 2025, focusing on 146 key suppliers representing highest spend and operational criticality. The program achieved 75% coverage through EcoVadis sustainability assessments and engaged suppliers across aircraft seats, engines, logistics and catering categories.

evidence.title: Supplier sustainability assessment program expansion
evidence.summary: IAG expanded its supplier engagement program in 2025, focusing on 146 key suppliers representing highest spend and operational criticality. The program achieved 75% coverage through EcoVadis sustainability assessments and engaged suppliers across aircraft seats, engines, logistics and catering categories.
evidence.quote: In 2025, we implemented a new strategy focusing on 146 key suppliers – those representing the highest spend and operational criticality. During the reporting year, we received seven new key supplier assessments. We achieved 75% coverage of our key suppliers through EcoVadis's sustainability assessments.

initiatives.name: Aer Lingus Manchester Base Strategic Closure
initiatives.summary: Following a strategic review, Aer Lingus decided to fully cease Manchester transatlantic operations and redeploy assets aligned with strategic priorities. This represents a significant operational restructuring of the airline's UK operations.

evidence.title: Aer Lingus Manchester base closure
evidence.summary: Following a strategic review, Aer Lingus decided to fully cease Manchester transatlantic operations and redeploy assets aligned with strategic priorities. This represents a significant operational restructuring of the airline's UK operations.
evidence.quote: In January 2026, following a review of the long-term viability of the Manchester Base, a decision was taken to fully cease Manchester transatlantic operations and redeploy the assets aligned with strategic priorities.

initiatives.name: Executive Remuneration Sustainability Linkage
initiatives.summary: IAG has implemented sustainability-linked annual incentives for over 7,500 senior executives and managers, with up to 10% of annual bonuses tied to carbon efficiency measures (gCO2/pkm) to support carbon intensity reduction ambitions.

evidence.title: Carbon efficiency executive remuneration targets
evidence.summary: IAG has implemented sustainability-linked annual incentives for over 7,500 senior executives and managers, with up to 10% of annual bonuses tied to carbon efficiency measures (gCO2/pkm) to support carbon intensity reduction ambitions.
evidence.quote: IAG has a number of sustainability-linked annual incentives for over 7,500 senior executives and managers across the Group, including 100% of IAG senior executives. These incentives are designed to support IAG's ambition to reduce the carbon intensity of its operations.

initiatives.name: Flightpath Net Zero Strategy
initiatives.summary: IAG has committed to achieving net zero emissions across Scope 1, 2 and 3 by 2050, with interim targets including 20% reduction in net Scope 1 and 3 emissions by 2030. The strategy includes fleet renewal, sustainable aviation fuel adoption, and carbon removals.

evidence.title: Investment in Breakthrough Energy Ventures SAF fund
evidence.summary: In September 2025, IAG invested alongside oneworld alliance member airlines in Breakthrough Energy Ventures to launch a new investment fund designed to address the limited availability and high cost of sustainable aviation fuel.
evidence.quote: In September 2025, IAG invested alongside oneworld alliance member airlines in Breakthrough Energy Ventures (BEV) to launch a new investment fund designed to address the limited availability and high cost of today's SAF.

evidence.title: Flightpath Net Zero strategy with 2050 targets
evidence.summary: IAG has committed to achieving net zero emissions across Scope 1, 2 and 3 by 2050, with interim targets including 20% reduction in net Scope 1 and 3 emissions by 2030. The strategy includes fleet renewal, sustainable aviation fuel adoption, and carbon removals.
evidence.quote: IAG is targeting net zero emissions by 2050 across its Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions.

initiatives.name: Shareholder Returns Program
initiatives.summary: Following completion of a €1 billion share buyback in 2025, IAG announced an additional €1.5 billion excess cash return to shareholders over the next 12 months. This reflects confidence in long-term prospects and disciplined capital allocation approach.

evidence.title: €1.5 billion share buyback program announced
evidence.summary: Following completion of a €1 billion share buyback in 2025, IAG announced an additional €1.5 billion excess cash return to shareholders over the next 12 months. This reflects confidence in long-term prospects and disciplined capital allocation approach.
evidence.quote: Building on our 2024 and 2025 share buyback programmes, we have announced a further return of excess cash of €1.5 billion in the next 12 months.

initiatives.name: Starlink In-Flight Connectivity Partnership
initiatives.summary: IAG announced partnership to implement Starlink-enabled high-speed Wi-Fi connectivity on all airline aircraft (Aer Lingus, British Airways, Iberia, LEVEL and Vueling). This will provide customers with download and upload speeds comparable to home connectivity, enabling streaming and online gaming.

evidence.title: Starlink Wi-Fi connectivity across all aircraft

This will provide customers with download and upload speeds comparable to home connectivity, enabling streaming and online gaming.
evidence.quote: In November we announced a partnership to implement Starlink-enabled high-speed Wi-Fi connectivity on Aer Lingus, British Airways, Iberia, LEVEL and Vueling aircraft.

initiatives.name: CFO Succession Planning
initiatives.summary: Nicholas Cadbury will step down as Chief Financial and Sustainability Officer in June 2026, to be succeeded by José Antonio Barrionuevo, currently Chief Financial and Transformation Officer at British Airways. This represents internal succession planning and leadership development.

evidence.title: CFO succession - José Antonio Barrionuevo appointed
evidence.summary: Nicholas Cadbury will step down as Chief Financial and Sustainability Officer in June 2026, to be succeeded by José Antonio Barrionuevo, currently Chief Financial and Transformation Officer at British Airways. This represents internal succession planning and leadership development.
evidence.quote: In January 2026, we announced that Nicholas Cadbury would be stepping down from his role in June 2026. José Antonio Barrionuevo has been appointed as his successor and he brings a strong track record in financial leadership and transformation in the aviation sector.

initiatives.name: Waste Reduction Strategy Refresh
initiatives.summary: IAG reviewed its waste strategy in 2025 and set new targets for delivery by 2030, including reducing virgin single-use plastics by 50% on a kg/ASK basis, reducing total waste generation per unit of activity by 10%, and achieving 80% appropriate waste disposal for recycling.

evidence.title: Extended waste reduction targets to 2030
evidence.summary: IAG reviewed its waste strategy in 2025 and set new targets for delivery by 2030, including reducing virgin single-use plastics by 50% on a kg/ASK basis, reducing total waste generation per unit of activity by 10%, and achieving 80% appropriate waste disposal for recycling.
evidence.quote: In 2025, IAG reviewed its waste strategy and extended this plan to 2030, setting new targets and updating our baseline to reflect current waste practices following the COVID-19 pandemic and operational changes incorporated into our operations.
